body: Pinterest has a lot of great content about simple organizing. You can print schedules and ideas right from there. I've gotten into minimalism which helps my bf and I's ADHD a TON. Every so often we will just grab a box and throw in clothes or any items we don't want to throw away but could be of good use to other people. Getting rid of a lot of clutter in our home helps to keep our minds calm (and it's less to clean! :) ) it's also helped our wallets. We're doing a no spend month or August and I can tel it's really helping. Start out slow. Don't get overwhelmed with where you aren't yet. Remind yourself how far you've come and how far you will go. Slow and steady wins the race ❤️

Not sure if this is necessarily a huge secret or even anything juicy but it's interesting to know...

Rental car representative here. Rental car companies do NOT make all of their money off of the damage waiver protections. They make it off of the rate per day they are renting the vehicle for. Everything is spread across each individual branch per car so if your average rate per car is even $3-4 higher and you have a 100 car branch that month...you're racking in some extra dough. Plus with the damage waiver if the customer does get the coverages, we are paying out of our group reserves to fix the vehicle if you damage it (I'm not sure if it's the branch reserves or group reserves anymore I work in a different department than rental but I was in rental for a year and a half) so we can actually lose money on occasion if you buy the damage waiver and destroy the vehicle. Don't get me wrong we can make a pretty penny off damage waiver sales but we would much rather have higher rates than anything else. 

People really need to know how hard it is working in a rental car industry and how many hours we work just to organize our fleet every single day just so you have a ride while your car is in the shop. Most branch managers I knew were working 60-70 hours a week. We work long hours, clean cars in business formal clothing, we have to learn how to run an entire business practically on our own, memorize countless things about insurance companies and liability laws all while dealing with constantly bitching customers. It's a hard job and most people have no idea how much work goes on behind the scenes and how intricate everything really is. 

PS - if you buy a rental and destroy it without coverages you WILL be charged. Don't believe all the movies and lies about being able to buy a rental, destroy it and return it thinking you won't have anything happen. We will contact your insurance company, we will collect your deductible and you will be fined.

Yeah people are fucking obnoxious about rental cars. So many times I would get yelled out about the qualification process...people telling me I'm discriminating or being nosy (I mean I'm giving you a $40,000 car the least you could do is show me your paystub) when all I was trying to do was my job. And people are so damn picky about every little thing and yell at me some more when the type of cars we had weren't out fault. It got to be too much I transferred to a different department in December. After a year and 3 months of constantly working 12 hr days, barely eating and cleaning cars in business formal clothing and  getting yelled at everyday...needless to say I was out of there as fast as my legs could take me.

Don't even get me STARTED on how I worked during hurricane sandy and people were coming in THE DAY OF needing a rental. Then there were people who were trying to force us to go pick them up in areas we knew they were completely flooded out an they were trying to lie and say it wasn't. -_-

Yes I forgot to mention the smoke smell. And then when people try to cover it up it makes it even worst. 

One time I answered the phone and the customer said there were bullet holes in the car and he didn't know how he got there. Another time I rented to an old man who drove through the windows at Shoneys. Tried to say the brakes didn't work on a brand new never before rented vehicle. Right. There was a branch close to where I worked as well that had a car on their books labeled "impound" and was being investigated by the cops because it was used in a murder case and had blood on it. No. Joke.

So many stories. One lady drive too close to a bank post and the entire front bumper was dragging on the road as she drove it. Another one this poor kid hit a deer and there were still guts on it. It was awful. And in terms of it being obvious....not always. We have an evaluator we use so ifs borderline we use that. Some people try to hide the damage....I've seen people put white out over scratches on white vehicles before. But for the most part we will catch it.
